article.title: Participios pasados got/gotten
article.part: Registro, variación y norma — Register, variation, and standard usage
article.chapter: Variedades del inglés — Varieties of English

claims.summary: The irregular verb get has variant past participles got and gotten. British English generally uses got where American English commonly uses gotten for becoming, receiving or acquiring (has got better versus has gotten better), while stative possessive have got is established in both varieties. Gotten in American English ordinarily expresses acquisition or change rather than the simple possessive state of have got.

links.notes: Registered reference covers irregular past participles of get and possessive have got in BrE and AmE.
